subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules and heartbeat config, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while limiting anti-herd behavior to heartbeat phases and cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config/protocol shape; repository policy treats those surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and automation should not choose the API/default contract alone.

options.title: Design a narrow `every` phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit opt-in contract for cron `every` and heartbeat scheduling with schema, CLI/protocol/docs, persistence, observability, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep `every` fixed
options.body: Close or mark not planned for cron `every` jitter/prime behavior, preserving fixed interval semantics and relying on existing heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger.

options.title: Accept a broader prime mode
options.body: Define prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron as a larger product surface with migration and rollout requirements.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow `every` phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit opt-in contract for cron `every` and heartbeat scheduling with schema, CLI/protocol/docs, persistence, observability, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the current cron-expression stagger boundary and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether cron `every` gets a new public timing contract.
